name: Learn a one-handed card cut
blurb: The Charlier cut — the deck splits, rotates and reassembles in one hand — takes a week to be reliable and looks like a lifetime of practice.
gear: A deck of cards, slightly worn is easier at first
steps: Hold the deck in dealer’s grip and let your thumb release the bottom half so it falls into your fingers.
Push the lower packet upward with your index finger so it clears the top packet.
Let the top packet fall onto your palm and drop the raised packet on top of it.
Do the whole move slowly, over a table, until the sequence is muscle memory.
Speed it up and remove the table.
Practise it on the other hand too — a two-handed display is far more striking.
tips: Do it over a bed for the first few days; you will drop the deck a hundred times.
The move is a controlled fall, not a squeeze. Fighting the deck makes it worse.
proof: Ten consecutive Charlier cuts, standing, no drops.
